query: For high-entropy alloys in demanding engineering applications, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve resistance to thermally induced toughness loss, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies an experiment that could falsify it?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a coherent L12 phase as a strengthener in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can improve their resistance to thermally induced toughness loss.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with a single solid-solution phase
generation.intervention: Introduction of a coherent L12 phase as a strengthener
generation.mechanism: Load transfer mechanism and suppression of radiation-induced segregation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved resistance to thermally induced toughness loss and enhanced mechanical properties
generation.baseline: HEAs without the coherent L12 phase
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing conditions required to introduce the coherent L12 phase are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of HEAs with and without the coherent L12 phase at elevated temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of the coherent L12 phase does not improve the resistance to thermally induced toughness loss, the hypothesis is falsified
